visual_system_craft.critique: The hero title 'AETHERVEIL' is clipped on the right: the final 'L' is cut off by the overlapping summoning-circle graphic, a clear construction/collision failure. The two-column hero is unbalanced—the left text block is tightly packed while the right is dominated by a large circle that intrudes into the title's line box, breaking the grid and alignment rhythm. The gold accent is applied inconsistently: the title uses a cream-to-gold gradient, the SUMMON button is a solid gold fill, the currency pill is gold, and the 'VEIL IS THINNING' eyebrow is teal—four different treatments of the same semantic accent with no clear rule. Typography scale is uneven: the hero H1 is enormous while the 'THE SANCTUM' section header is comparatively small and under-weighted, weakening the hierarchy step between hero and section. The stat row (TOTAL POWER / SPIRITS / WIN STREAK) uses thin vertical dividers that don't align to a consistent baseline or spacing grid, and the '/ 240' sub-label sits at a different optical weight than its neighbors. The bottom cards are cut off mid-frame with no visible card body, leaving an unfinished region; their corner brackets and icon chips are present but the card fill, border, and content are not yet legible, so the component grammar is incomplete. The top nav's server pill, currency pill, and avatar use three different border/radius treatments that don't read as one system.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: 1) Fix the title clipping immediately: either constrain the hero circle to the right column with a defined gutter so the H1 has full line width, or reduce the H1 size / shift the circle right so no glyph is occluded. 2) Establish a single accent rule: reserve gold for primary/interactive and value emphasis (SUMMON, currency, key numbers) and teal for secondary/ambient (eyebrow, bound-count, icons); apply the same gold as a flat fill or a single consistent gradient, not both. 3) Rebuild the hero on a 12-col grid with a fixed left text column and right art column, aligning the H1, eyebrow, body, buttons, and stat row to a shared left margin and baseline grid. 4) Normalize the type scale: set a modular scale so H1 → section H2 → body → label steps are deliberate (e.g., H1 96, H2 40, body 18, label 12) with consistent weights and letter-spacing. 5) Unify the stat row: equal column widths, consistent divider height/opacity, and aligned baselines; make '/ 240' a muted sub-label at a defined smaller size. 6) Complete the bottom cards: define a single card component (fill, 1px border, radius, corner-bracket accent, icon chip, label, and value pill) and ensure all four cards render fully within the viewport with consistent internal padding. 7) Standardize the top-nav pills: one radius, one border color/opacity, and one internal spacing token across server, currency, and avatar.
